mainEntity.name: What should happen when an AI support bot cannot answer a customer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Set escalation rules before launch, including what the AI must recognize, what information it must pass along, and who receives the handoff. A useful handoff contains the original conversation, customer history, detected issue, sources consulted, confidence concerns, and a suggested next step. Context: Community examples emphasize escalation with context rather than simply transferring an unanswered message. That prevents the customer from repeating the problem and gives the reviewer a usable starting point. Key factors: - urgency - customer sentiment - policy exceptions - missing or conflicting data - channel response hours. Practical guidance: Test handoffs with angry, vague, multi-part, and off-topic messages. Add a fallback for system outages so customers can still reach a person or receive a clear delay notice. Review failed escalations as carefully as incorrect answers.
acceptedAnswer.description: The workflow should stop guessing and hand the case to a person with the full conversation, customer history, issue category, missing information, and suggested next step. Test vague, angry, multi-part, and outage-related messages before launch, and provide a clear fallback channel.
